literal: At that time Zhengcang's younger brother Zhengyi had presented himself as Presented Scholar and Zhenglun as Outstanding Talent—the three brothers answered the summons together, and the age sighed in admiration.
idiomatic: Then Zhengcang's brother Zhengyi had presented himself as Presented Scholar and Zhenglun as Outstanding Talent—the three brothers answered together, and the age admired them.

literal: Court Gentleman for the Imperial Compilation Wang Shao memorialized to pursue revision of the histories; Minister of Grain Xue Daohang memorialized to draft them as staff—both were in current posts and were sent home for the time being.
idiomatic: Compilation Gentleman Wang Shao memorialized to revise the histories; Grain Minister Xue Daohang memorialized staff—all were in post and sent home for now.

literal: In the ninth year he followed the imperial progress on the Liaodong campaign as Chief Clerk on the Fuyu Route army.
idiomatic: In year 9 he followed the Liaodong campaign as Chief Clerk on the Fuyu Route.

literal: On return he reached Zhuo commandery and died.
idiomatic: On return he reached Zhuo commandery and died.

literal: Zhengcang composed with speed, as though the text had been prepared overnight.
idiomatic: Zhengcang wrote with speed, as though prepared overnight.

literal: Once he had several men each hold brush and paper, each set a topic for an essay; Zhengcang dictated and all were completed at once, each with literary order—men of the time marveled.
idiomatic: Once he set several men with brush and paper, each with a topic; Zhengcang dictated and all were finished at once, each ordered—his age marveled.

literal: He also wrote Literary Tracks in twenty scrolls, discussing the norms of literary form, with very clear arrangement.
idiomatic: He also wrote Literary Tracks in twenty scrolls on literary norms, very clearly arranged.

literal: Later students treasured and practiced it; many relied on it to leave the purple, and it spread greatly in the world—called the New Book of the Du House.
idiomatic: Later students treasured it; many relied on it to leave the purple, and it spread widely—called the New Book of the Du House.

literal: The historians comment: Song Yin's conduct was pure and white, leaving glory and name behind;
idiomatic: The historians comment: Song Yin's conduct was pure white, leaving glory behind;

literal: Xuan and Yin both preserved withdrawal and simplicity and were all summoned to office—houses of virtue, indeed.
idiomatic: Xuan and Yin both preserved withdrawal and simplicity and were summoned to office—houses of virtue indeed.

literal: Yihe was known for talent and measure, his traces joining in entrusted counsel; standing out above the crowd—there must have been cause!
idiomatic: Yihe was known for talent; his traces joined entrusted counsel; standing above the crowd—there was cause!

literal: The sigh over having no son—is it only Yangshe's!
idiomatic: The sigh over no son—is it only Yangshe's!

literal: That the ancestral sacrifices did not perish was perhaps their fortune.
idiomatic: That ancestral sacrifice did not perish was perhaps fortune.

literal: Fan was upright and independent, fierce in cutting through affairs.
idiomatic: Fan was upright and independent, fierce in affairs.

literal: Shiliang and his brothers, refined in family style.
idiomatic: Shiliang and his brothers refined the family style.

literal: Daomo reached eminence through divination; Jiliang was hindered by shallow learning.
idiomatic: Daomo reached eminence through divination; Jiliang was weighed down by shallow learning.

literal: Diao Yong's talent and vision were broad and far; he won fame in founding affairs, received preferential treatment, and for generations held human rank—the meaning of building the hall.
idiomatic: Diao Yong's talent was broad and far; he won fame, received honor, and for generations held rank—the meaning of building the hall.

literal: The Xin and Wei houses did not let their gate's wind perish.
idiomatic: Xin and Wei did not let their gate's wind perish.

literal: Wherever Du Quan stood, he was held in weight.
idiomatic: Wherever Du Quan stood, men gave him weight.

literal: Zhengxuan—hard to say which brother excels; truly beautiful!
idiomatic: Zhengxuan—hard to say which brother excels; beautiful indeed!
